situation:
You are the operations manager of PANTRY POST, a subscription company that ships a box of small-batch snacks to a subscriber's door every month. Two difficult years cost the company half its list and most of its shelf partners. A new managing partner (judge) took over eight months ago, cut the product line back to one box, and has brought the business to steady ground again.

PANTRY POST packs everything by hand in a shared commercial kitchen that rents the company twenty hours a week under a signed agreement, and those twenty hours are now full. You and the managing partner (judge) are the only two people who pack. Between the two of you, four hundred boxes a month is the ceiling, and the company has reached it.

Two kinds of customers fill those boxes. Individual subscribers pay month to month, film their own unboxing videos for social feeds, and brought most of the new names in during the recovery. Three local employers hold corporate gift accounts that fill the rest of the packing hours, pay a third of monthly revenue, and underwrite the box PANTRY POST donates to a school food pantry for every ten it ships.

Growth from either group now needs more hands. Hiring the first employee, a full-time packer, would lift the ceiling, but it adds a fixed monthly salary and spends the cash reserve the turnaround set aside to restock inventory after the holidays. Holding off and dropping the corporate gift accounts frees those packing hours for subscribers, but costs a third of monthly revenue and ends the school food pantry donation the accounts underwrite.

The managing partner (judge) has asked you to recommend whether to hire the first employee or to drop the corporate gift accounts, and to explain what your recommendation does to how PANTRY POST is promoted and to whom. The managing partner (judge) will greet you, ask to hear your ideas, and will thank you after your presentation and questions.
judgeCharacterization:

You took the company over eight months ago after two difficult years and you have it steady again. You want the operations manager's recommendation on whether to hire the first employee or to drop the corporate gift accounts, and you want to hear what that recommendation does to the way the company reaches customers.
